subject: Morning edition, Tuesday, Sep 29: President Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen…

items.text: President Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the war.
items.detail: Iran had offered terms to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the route for about a fifth of the world's oil shipments, and end the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, now in its seventh month. Iran's foreign minister said Iran will wait for a formal U.S. response before abandoning ceasefire talks. Eight U.S. Marines were injured by an Iranian missile in the strait on Sept. 14.
items.why: Determines whether an active war involving the U.S. continues and whether a key global oil route reopens.

items.text: The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.2% on Sept. 28, its highest level in 19 years, and U.S. crude oil rose 4.2% to $96.31 a barrel after President Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
items.detail: All three major stock indexes closed lower: the S&P 500 fell 0.77% to 7,683.69, the Dow 0.67% and the Nasdaq 0.92%. Brent crude briefly traded above $108 before settling near $98. The 10-year yield is a benchmark for mortgage and other long-term loan rates.
items.why: A 19-year high in the 10-year yield pushes up mortgage and loan rates nationwide; oil prices feed directly into gas prices.

items.text: President Trump announced at 2:00 p.m. that Mesabi Metallics, owned by India-based Essar Group, plans a $15 billion steel mill in eastern Iowa, using ore from its mine near Nashwauk, Minnesota.
items.detail: The mill would use iron ore from Mesabi Metallics' new mine near Nashwauk on Minnesota's Iron Range, which opened this month; the mine has hired over 200 of a planned 350 workers. Mesabi Metallics is owned by India-based Essar Group. No construction start date or mill job count was given.
items.why: A $15 billion private investment in U.S. steel capacity. Rated 3 rather than higher because it is a plan, not yet under construction.

items.text: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran is waiting for an official U.S. response before ending ceasefire talks; an Iranian official said Iran will not change its position on its nuclear program.
items.detail: The statements followed the U.S. rejection of Iran's proposal. An Iranian army spokesman also said Iran's forces are prepared for renewed U.S. attacks.
items.why: Shows where ceasefire talks stand, but is a statement of position, not a decision or action.

items.text: SpaceX's Starship reached orbit for the first time on its 14th test flight Monday, deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites.
items.detail: The ship completed about six orbits over roughly 10 hours before splashing down in the Pacific west of Chile; the Super Heavy booster splashed down in the Gulf shortly after launch. SpaceX changed the booster after ice buildup caused problems on the previous flight. NASA plans to use a modified Starship as the moon lander for its Artemis program.
items.why: A first for the largest rocket built and a step required before NASA's planned Artemis moon landings; still a test program.

also.text: The MLB regular season ended Sunday with the 12-team playoff field set. The Wild Card Series start Tuesday, Sept. 29.
also.detail: Top seeds with byes: Rays (AL East, 98-64) and Guardians (AL Central) in the AL; Brewers (NL Central, 103-59) and defending champion Dodgers (NL West, 100-62) in the NL. Best-of-three matchups: Astros vs. White Sox, Yankees vs. Red Sox, Braves vs. Phillies, Padres vs. Cubs, with any deciding games by Oct. 1.
also.why: Sets the postseason bracket for Major League Baseball.

also.text: AMD agreed to buy World Labs, the AI startup founded by Stanford professor Fei-Fei Li, for $8.2 billion.
also.detail: World Labs builds AI models of the physical world; its first product, Marble, generates simulated environments for entertainment and robot training. Li will become AMD's executive vice president and chief scientist. The deal is expected to close by year-end, subject to regulatory approval.
also.why: A large AI acquisition by a major chipmaker; it still needs regulatory approval.

upcoming.text: MLB Wild Card Series begin (best of three).
Federal fiscal year ends; government stays funded through Dec. 11 under the stopgap law.
